verified_fixes: Guard: I ran guard.sh on 4f2add8 myself and it printed GUARD: ALL GREEN. That covers fmt, clippy -D warnings, all tests, doctests, MSRV 1.75, wasm and rustdoc -D warnings.

A (the blocking item from round 3) is fixed. Nothing painted falls off the canvas any more. I surveyed 9362 SVGs from 116 inputs: the 14 flowchart corpus files, state, examples/*.mmd, tests/fixtures/quality, 6 stress inputs of mine (y1-y6) and 80 seeded random flowcharts of mine (rnd/q00-q79). Each input was rendered as static, as route() fed the static centres, as 16 drag frames through route, route_partial on a routed base and route_partial on the static base, and as 48 'near' frames with a target 0.5-9 px from its source. Two independent checks: (1) numeric, every edge path's curve sampled with half its stroke out plus every marker box against the viewBox: 1055 clipped before this round (05d93b3), 0 now; (2) pixel, Chromium render with overflow visible, counting any ink outside the viewBox: 0 of 9362 now. The pixel check does catch the old clipping: it flags 59 of 60 known-clipped pre-round renders, advanced.routed among them. The folded/compact canvas and the advance outputs are clean too.

Quality: defect totals are unchanged (static 69, routed 98). Against 05d93b3, every B0 metric except width/height/ink/aspect is byte-for-byte the same on every corpus file. Width and height grow by 24 (padding 16 -> 28), plus route growth on advanced and bench-75 routed. Against the pre-package 519b38c the deltas are the ones round 3 already accepted.

Drag budget per PLAN invariant 1 (two perf.sh runs, v-b1-arrows-r4 and -r4-2). bench-75 drag 23.31/22.25 (limit 25.28), route 13.19/11.38 (limit 15.76). dense-td drag 13.26/12.85, dense-lr drag 13.11/13.56, both within budget. wide-labels drag was 4.18 on run 1, over its 3.89 limit, and 2.67 on the re-run: noise (earlier runs range 2.71-4.39). route_partial max is 5.23 ms on bench-75 in my interactive run. Static scene_ms is well within 2x everywhere. to_svg (bench files, min ms, 05d93b3 -> now): bench-75 34.8->32.9, dense-lr 24.9->25.3, dense-td 24.4->27.0.

B (short curves) is fixed for normal strokes. I compared every painted arrow tip (from the path end, refX and markerWidth) with the scene curve's end, about 310k heads, including near frames 0.5-12 px apart, horizontal and vertical. Static and routed tips sit within about 1 px of the end; before this round the drag frames had 10279 heads more than 1 px off, now 387 (see notes). Shrunk heads get arrow-t0-s<len> ids, and a 0.5 px gap draws no head.

C works up to about 14 px. The x1_styles 14 px stroke (the case flagged in round 3) now ends in a 22.5 px head with its tip on the border and no butt shoulders (zoom/x1_side.png). Strokes up to 12 px and the thick 3.5 px edge keep the 11 px head (arrow_head_len == 11 for widths up to 6). The advance painter grows its head the same way: a 24 px advance edge gets a 37.5 px head with its tip on the border (zoom/adv_v.png).
Earlier fixes still hold: thick head == normal head, square heads, crowded heads narrowed (arrow-w), crossing gaps clear of heads, and advance outputs byte-identical to 05d93b3.

Non-flowchart renderers are byte-identical to both 519b38c and 05d93b3, in cmp/corpus and examples: class, er, sequence, pie, journey, timeline, gitgraph, sankey, mindmap, architecture. The advance-text examples are byte-identical to 05d93b3.

Interactive contract (scratch crate ix4/ix4n outside the repo, all 116 inputs, every frame listed above): SceneEdge stays index-parallel with Graph::edges in every frame, including near frames; scene, route, route_partial and to_svg are deterministic (byte-equal when run twice); the to_mermaid round-trip is unchanged on every input. Picking: tol-0 on-stroke probes missed 1 of 110k (static) and 0 of 110k (routed); random probes disagreed 190 and 192 times out of about 325k each, concentrated on the wide-stroke heads in the problem below.

Tests are not weakened. Every assertion removed since 519b38c reappears elsewhere or was replaced for a documented id/token change (arrow-u gone, 3.4 -> 3.5, a dash check reworded to the attribute). There is no #[ignore]. ink_out is gated at 0. New tests: nothing_painted_falls_off_the_canvas, a_curve_shorter_than_its_cut_keeps_its_head_on_it, a_very_wide_stroke_ends_inside_its_grown_head. No new dependency and no debug leftovers. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] (Q10 wording, canvas fix, head growth and shrink, ink_out breaking note) and the README linkStyle paragraph are updated.
problems: BLOCKING (new regression from rescue C, src/scene.rs arrow_trim / arrow_head_len ~1990-2010 with the square_end fallback ~1590-1640): very wide linkStyle strokes (about 15 px and over) now paint their grown head with the tip off the node border, in static and routed renders. The cap on the cut is gone (cut = width, head = 1.5*width + 1.5). Where square_end cannot give the grown head its straight run (a back-edge bow, a routed turn near the end, an S-cubic), the stroke is still cut a full width back, and the head points along the curve's tangent at that cut, so its tip misses the end point. Tip vs scene-curve end, static/routed, over my 116 inputs: 05d93b3 max 4.2/5.7 px (one pre-existing case, the 12 px edge in y2_widetd); 4f2add8 has 15 static and 17 routed heads more than 1 px off, max 19.2 px. Examples (marker id, error): rnd/q53 routed n2->n4 arrow-t24-s37_5 19.2 px; the head points left at empty space below n4 and never touches it (zoom/q53_head.png). ex/y2_widetd static c->a arrow-t24-s37_5 19.2 px; the head floats below Alpha inside the frame (zoom/y2_static.png). rnd/q44 routed 18.7 px. ex/y1_wide static A->C (40 px) 13 px off Target two, with a hooked base (zoom/y1_static.png). rnd/q04 static n0<==>n5 (24 px) 9.5 px at both ends: the painted path is just 'M 386.5 121.9 C ... 367.1 91.6' and both 37.5 px heads face along the S-curve's middle. rnd/q43 static (16 px) 6.2 px; the tip sits in empty space beside the parallelogram (zoom/q43_head.png). In drag frames it reaches 37.7 px (q66). This also breaks pick == render on those heads: the painter adds head ink where picking does not reach. y2_widetd static has a tol-0 miss on the painted stroke at (99.3,120.5), and random probes on the painted heads return None or another edge (q04: 131 mismatches, y2_widetd: 54). Both inputs are in verify/b1-arrows/r4/ex and r4/rnd. The lead required 'very wide linkStyle strokes end cleanly at the head' and 'tips on borders' to stay fixed. This is not the deferred S-cubic elbow: the tip itself leaves the border by up to 19 px, and y2_widetd and q53 are routed waypoint paths, not single cubics. Suggested fix: when square_end finds no straight run as long as the grown head, do not grow (or cut) beyond what the end allows. For example, grow the head only up to the straight run actually achieved, keeping the pre-rescue capped cut otherwise, or keep the tip on the end point by orienting the head from the cut to the end. Add a test that the painted tip equals the scene curve's end for 16/24/40 px strokes on a back-edge bow, an S-cubic and a routed turn (ex/m1_back24.mmd, y2_widetd, q53).
unfixed_items: C for strokes of about 15 px and over: the grown head's tip leaves the border on turning ends (blocking problem above). 14 px and under is fine.

Q10 MARGIN 16: the 28 px gutter is kept, and the SVG now pads like the scene. The skip is legitimate: the lead allowed it once a test proves nothing clips, and both nothing_painted_falls_off_the_canvas and my 9362-SVG survey show 0 clipped. The stated cost (translations flip the router's float tie-breaks) is plausible.
Exact static canvas fit (Q2) is left to B2. Legitimate: it was not part of B1, the Scene canvas always contains the SVG canvas, and nothing clips.

Elbows at the head base of strongly turning single S-cubics (deferred to B10), routed ports-stage end angles (B7), the router's longer end stub (dropped) and to_svg on large synthetic graphs (within the 2x budget): deferrals the lead accepted. The implementer stretched the elbow deferral to cover 'a very wide stroke's curl into its grown head'; that covers the curl, but not tips leaving the border.
notes:
Verdict is fail on one blocking item: very wide linkStyle strokes (about 15 px and over) now land their grown head off the target's border in static and routed renders, by up to 19 px. This round introduced it. Everything else checks out.

**What checks out**
- **A (canvas):** solidly fixed. 0 of 9362 SVGs clip now, on both the numeric and the pixel check; 1055 did before this round.
- **B (short curves):** fixed. Normal-stroke tips sit on the curve's end in static and routed renders.
- **C at 8-14 px:** the stroke ends inside its head.
- Guard is green and perf is within budget.
- Quality metrics are identical to 05d93b3 apart from canvas size.
- Non-flowchart and advance outputs are byte-identical.
- The interactive contract holds.

**Non-blocking**
1. Normal strokes in degenerate drag frames: 387 of about 300k heads are more than 1 px off their curve's end, max 10.9 px.
   - Worst case: rnd/q44, node moved 4.5 px below its neighbour, n1->n6 path `M 498.1 260.0 C 498.1 240.3, 498.1 280.2, 498.1 281.9`. It is a collinear cubic that overshoots its end; trimming 5.5 px of arc lands on the overshoot, so the head points past the end.
   - The worst case is identical before this round (that run had 10279 such heads); it is not caused by the rescue.
2. `Metrics::ink_out` is nearly tautological. It measures painted ink against the same grow_canvas bounds the canvas is built from, so it can only catch a stray of more than 28 px. The real guard is the SVG-parsing test, which is good.
3. A static scene whose drawing reaches into the gutter is now translated by up to about 14 px. Hosts see shifted static coordinates. This is documented in the CHANGELOG and only a translation.
4. A phantom node `e1` appears when `e1@{ curve: step }` names no edge (x1_styles). It is the same at 05d93b3, so not this round's.
5. Side-by-side pages that inline several flowmaid SVGs share marker ids such as `arrow`, so one SVG's markers can resolve to another's. I relied only on single-SVG renders (zoom.js) for evidence.

- I removed my pre/prer worktrees. The repo is untouched: HEAD 4f2add8, clean.
